title: Baking With My Grandpa: Sugar Cookies And A Cake

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Hey Grandpa, I cleared my whole afternoon so we could bake together. I was thinking we could make those sugar cookies you used to make with Mom.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Oh, you want to film a baking tutorial? I didn't know you had a channel. Should I put on an apron and smile for the camera?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: No, no camera. I just want us to spend time together and maybe you could show me the recipe. Like, actually do it together.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I see, you want me to perform for an audience. I can be entertaining if that's what you're looking for. Should I tell some jokes while we mix?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Grandpa, I'm not looking for entertainment. I want to learn from you. I miss doing things together like we used to.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So you're saying I don't spend enough time with you? I didn't realize you were keeping score. I thought we saw each other just last month.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: That's not what I meant at all. I just thought baking would be a nice way to reconnect. I didn't mean to make you feel guilty.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Well, if you feel guilty, that's on you. I never asked you to clear your afternoon. You could have just called if you wanted to talk.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I did call. Three times this week. You kept saying you were busy. I thought showing up in person would show I really care.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now you're tracking my schedule? I didn't realize I needed to report my whereabouts. I have a life outside of waiting by the phone.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I wasn't tracking you. I was just trying to plan something nice. Can we please just start with the flour and sugar?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want me to do all the work while you watch? Fine, I'll get the flour. But don't expect me to do a professional demonstration.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I want to HELP. I want us to do it together. I'll measure, you guide me. That's what I came here for.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want me to boss you around? I don't like being that kind of grandfather. If you want orders, watch a cooking show.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't want orders. I want guidance. There's a difference. Like, when I was little, you'd hold my hand while we stirred.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now you're saying I don't hold your hand enough? You're a grown woman. I thought you wanted to be treated like an adult.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I do want to be treated like an adult. But that doesn't mean I don't want your company. Why are you making this so hard?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I'm making it hard? You're the one with all the complaints. First I don't spend time, then I don't guide, then I don't hold your hand.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Those weren't complaints. They were explanations of what I was hoping for. I thought you'd be happy I wanted to learn from you.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Happy? You show up unannounced with a list of demands about how I should behave. That's not a visit, that's an inspection.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It wasn't unannounced. I told you Tuesday I'd be here Saturday. And there was no list. Just one request: bake together.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: And now you're correcting my memory. Great. So I'm old and forgetful on top of everything else. Thanks for the reminder.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't say you were old or forgetful. I just wanted to clarify. Can we please reset? I'll get the bowls. You get the recipe.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want me to find the recipe? I haven't used it in years. I thought you said you wanted to teach ME something new.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: When did I say that? I said I wanted to learn the recipe FROM you. You're the one who knows it.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now you're saying I don't know it well enough to teach? Make up your mind. Either I know it or I don't.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You DO know it. That's why I came. I want you to teach me because you know it. Why would I ask if I thought you didn't?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Maybe to test me. Maybe to see if the old man still has it. Well, I do. But I don't appreciate being tested in my own kitchen.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: There is no test. There is no camera. There is no audience. Just me, you, and some flour. Can we start?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Fine. But don't blame me if they don't turn out perfect. You seem to have very high expectations.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't need perfect. I just want to try. Can you tell me how much flour?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want exact measurements? Your mother never measured. She just felt it. I thought you wanted to be like her.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I do want to be like her. But I'm not her. I need measurements because I'm still learning. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So you're saying I'm a bad teacher because I don't measure? Some people learn by doing, not by numbers.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm not saying you're a bad teacher. I'm saying I learn differently. Can we do both? You feel, I measure?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want to do it your way and my way? That's twice the work. I thought this was supposed to be simple.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It can be simple. You do it your way. I'll watch and write down roughly how much you use. Then I'll try next batch.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So I'm the practice round? You want to observe me like I'm some experiment? I don't like being studied.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Not studied. Just watched. By someone who loves you. Why does everything I say sound like criticism to you?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Because you keep correcting me. 'Not that much flour, Grandpa. Not that way, Grandpa.' I can hear it already.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I haven't said any of that. I haven't even touched the flour yet. You're arguing with a version of me that doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now I'm imagining things? Perfect. Add delusional to the list. Old, forgetful, and delusional.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't say delusional. I said you're predicting I'll criticize you before I even do anything. That's not fair.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Life isn't fair. You want fair? Go to court. In my kitchen, we do things my way or not at all.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then let's do it your way. I'll just watch. No comments. No measuring. Just tell me what you're doing.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Now you want me to narrate? I thought you said no camera. Narrating is for shows. Make up your mind.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I just want to understand what you're doing. If you don't want to narrate, just do it and I'll ask after.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now I'm supposed to perform silently and then take questions? I'm not a professor. I'm a grandfather.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You're allowed to just be a grandfather. That's literally all I want. Just be yourself and bake with me.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Myself? You mean the old, forgetful, delusional version? The one who doesn't measure and doesn't narrate?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I never called you those things. You did. I called you Grandpa. The man who made cookies with Mom. That's who I see.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You see a memory. Not a person. The person in front of you is tired, his hands hurt, and he doesn't feel like performing.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then don't perform. Just exist. I'll do the physical work. You sit and tell me if I'm doing it right.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now I'm useless? You want me to sit in the corner like a decoration while you do everything?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I said your HANDS hurt. I was trying to be considerate. I wanted you involved without hurting yourself.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Considerate? You came here to tell me I'm too weak to mix dough. That's not considerate. That's pity.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It's not pity. It's love. I don't want you in pain. I want you here, with me, comfortable.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Love doesn't look like taking over someone's kitchen and telling them to sit down. Love looks like asking what THEY want.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: What do you want, then? Tell me. I'll do it. I just want us to have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I wanted to watch the game. I was looking forward to it all week. But sure, let's bake cookies instead.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You never told me there was a game. I would have come another time. Why didn't you say something?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Because you didn't ask. You announced. 'I'm coming Saturday.' There was no question mark in that text.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I thought you'd be happy to see me. I didn't realize I needed to schedule an appointment with my own grandfather.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You don't need an appointment. You need manners. A simple 'would Saturday work?' goes a long way.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Would Saturday have worked? Or would you have said no because of the game and then I'd feel like you didn't want to see me?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So you didn't ask because you were afraid of the answer? That's not planning. That's avoidance.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Maybe. But I also genuinely thought you'd want to see me. I guess I was wrong about that too.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Don't put words in my mouth. I do want to see you. I just wanted to see you AND watch the game. Now I get neither.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: We can watch the game while the dough chills. I don't need your full attention every second.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So now I'm supposed to divide my attention? You'll complain I'm not focused on you. I know how this goes.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I won't complain. I promise. Let's make the dough, put it in the fridge, and watch the game together.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Together? You'll ask questions during the best plays. You always do. 'Who's that? What's the rule?' I can't enjoy it.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I won't ask anything. I'll just sit there. Or I'll leave and come back after the game if you want to be alone.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Leave? So now you're threatening to walk out? Great. Emotional blackmail. Very mature.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It's not blackmail. It's giving you space. You said you wanted to watch the game. I'm offering to let you.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: And then you'll tell everyone I kicked you out on a Saturday. No thanks. I'll suffer through the baking.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I would never say that. Why do you think I'm going to betray you? When have I ever done that?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You told your mother I forgot her birthday. I didn't forget. I just didn't make a big deal about it.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't tell her. She asked me if you seemed okay, and I said you seemed quiet. That's all.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Quiet? So now I'm depressing too? Add that to the list. Old, forgetful, delusional, depressing.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You keep adding to that list. I don't have a list. I have one wish: to bake cookies with you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: One wish that comes with forty conditions. No camera, but narrate. No measuring, but write it down. No game, but watch together.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Those weren't conditions. They were attempts to compromise because you kept misunderstanding what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: So it's my fault? I'm the one who can't understand? Maybe you're just bad at explaining what you want.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Maybe I am. But I've explained it ten different ways and you hear something different every time.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Because your words don't match your actions. You say 'no pressure' but your voice is shaking with pressure.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: My voice is shaking because I'm frustrated. Because I came here to feel close to you and I feel further away than ever.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Further away? So this is my fault? I didn't ask for this visit. You imposed it and now you're disappointed I'm not magical?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't want magic. I wanted normal. I wanted flour on our hands and laughter. Not this... this argument.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You wanted laughter? Then tell a joke. Don't expect me to be a comedian just because you walked through the door.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't expect you to be a comedian. I expect you to want to be here with me. Do you?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Of course I do. But not like this. Not with you monitoring my every word for signs I don't love you.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm not monitoring. I'm reacting. Because your words DO hurt. They make me feel like a burden.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: A burden? You think I see you as a burden? You're my granddaughter. I love you. I just don't love being interrogated.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I wasn't interrogating. I was asking about cookies. How did that become an interrogation?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Because every question had a hidden test. 'Do you remember the recipe?' means 'Do you still have your mind?'

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It meant 'Do you remember the recipe?' Because I don't. And I wanted to learn it. Nothing more.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Fine. Two cups flour. One cup sugar. Half cup butter. One egg. Mix. Bake at three-fifty. Done.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Thank you. That helps. Should we cream the butter and sugar first, or melt the butter?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Now you're questioning my method? I just gave you the recipe and already you want to change it.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm not changing it. I'm asking for clarification. Mom said you creamed it. I just want to do it right.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Your mother said a lot of things. Some true, some not. You believe everything she tells you about me?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: She told me you were patient and kind. That you let her make mistakes. That you laughed when flour went everywhere.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: She remembers what she wants to remember. We had bad days too. She just chooses to forget them.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then help me make a good memory today. One we both want to remember. Please, Grandpa.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Please? Now you're begging? I don't want your pity-baking. If you want to leave, leave.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't want to leave. I want to stay. I want to fix this. I don't know how, but I want to.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Fix this? So this is broken? Our relationship is broken because we had one disagreement about butter?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It's not about butter. It's about intent. I came with good intent and you keep reading bad intent into everything.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Maybe because your good intent feels like pressure. 'Let's bond' is an order dressed as a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: What should I have said? What words would have made you feel safe instead of attacked?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I don't know. But 'I cleared my whole afternoon' sounds like an investment expecting returns.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: The return I wanted was your company. That's it. No cookies required. Just... you.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Just me? The old, forgetful, delusional, depressing me? You want that version?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I want the version that exists. However he is. However YOU are. Right now. In this kitchen.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: That's... that's a lot to sit with. I don't think anyone has said that to me in a very long time.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then let me say it again. I want to be here. With you. Not a memory. Not a performance. Just you.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Okay. But I need you to know... my hands do hurt. And I am tired. And I might not be fun.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You don't have to be fun. You just have to be honest. Tell me when it hurts. I'll do the mixing.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: And I need you to know... I did forget your mother's birthday. Not the date. Just to call. I felt awful.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I know. She knows. Everyone forgets sometimes. It doesn't make you awful. It makes you human.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I thought you were here to judge me for it. That's why I got defensive. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm sorry too. I should have asked about your week first. Instead I barged in with my plan.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Your plan wasn't bad. Just... sudden. Like a surprise exam I didn't study for.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: No more exams. No more hidden tests. Just cookies. Or no cookies. Whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Let's try the cookies. But you mix. I'll supervise. And if I fall asleep in the chair, don't wake me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Deal. But if you snore, I'm taking a video. Just kidding. No camera. I promise.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You joke about the camera, but I really did think you were filming. You had that excited energy.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: That was nervous energy. I was scared you'd say no. Or worse, say yes but not mean it.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I always mean it. Even when I'm grumpy. Especially when I'm grumpy. It means I care enough to argue.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then let's be grumpy together while we bake. Grumpy cookies. Worst cookies ever. On purpose.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: On purpose? So now you're planning to ruin them? This is a very strange baking strategy.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Not ruin. Just not stress about perfection. Ugly cookies taste the same. Maybe better.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Your mother said the same thing once. She burned a whole batch and called them 'rustic.'

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Rustic. I like that. Let's make rustic cookies. Extra rustic. Barely recognizable as cookies.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Now you're making fun of my recipe? I thought we were past the criticism phase.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Not making fun. Embracing imperfection. There's a difference. One hurts, one frees.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Frees. I like that word. I haven't felt free in a kitchen in a long time. Just... observed.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Who observes you? Mom? The nurses? Who makes you feel watched?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Everyone. Since your grandmother died, people watch to see if I'm coping. It's exhausting.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm not watching to see if you're coping. I'm watching because I miss you. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: It's more than okay. It's... it's why I agreed to Saturday even though there was a game.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You agreed because you wanted to see me? Even with the game?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I agreed because I love you. I just forgot how to say that without sounding annoyed.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You said it just fine. Let's make some ugly, rustic, grumpy cookies. Together.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Together. But if they're inedible, you're explaining it to your mother.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Fair. I'll tell her we were going for 'abstract cookie art.' She'll understand.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Abstract cookie art. I like the sound of that. Very sophisticated. Very... us.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay, two cups of flour. Should I sift it first?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want to sift? So my method of just dumping it in isn't good enough for you?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I just asked if I should sift. Some recipes say sift, some don't.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Now you're comparing my recipe to 'some recipes.' I see how it is.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm not comparing. I'm asking a practical question. The flour has lumps. Sifting removes lumps.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Lumps add character. Your mother never sifted and her cookies were perfect.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You just said Mom made mistakes. Now her cookies were perfect? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Both. She made mistakes but they turned out perfect. That's the magic of not overthinking.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: So I should just dump everything in and hope for magic? That's your advice?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: My advice is to relax. But you can't relax. You're treating this like a chemistry exam.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm treating it with respect. I want them to be good. Is that a crime?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Respect? You mean control. You want to control every variable so nothing surprises you.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I want to control the outcome because I care. Because I want you to taste them and smile.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I'll smile if you smile. Not if the cookies are perfect. You still don't get that.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I do get it. But I also want to be proud of what we made. Is pride not allowed?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Pride is allowed. But your pride looks like anxiety. And anxiety is contagious.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: So now I'm infecting you? Great. I'll try to be less contagious. Should I wear a mask?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Don't be dramatic. I'm saying your energy affects the room. Right now it's tense.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: It's tense because every question I ask becomes an argument. I asked about sifting.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: And I answered. No sifting. But you kept pushing. 'Lumps this, recipes that.'

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I was explaining my reasoning. So you'd understand where I was coming from.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I don't need your reasoning. I need your hands in the bowl. Less talking, more mixing.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: So now I talk too much? I came here to talk AND bake. Not be a silent kitchen robot.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: A silent kitchen robot? Is that how you see my requests? As demands for silence?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You said 'less talking, more mixing.' That's a demand for silence. Pretty clear.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: It's a request for focus. There's a difference. But you hear demands everywhere.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Because they keep coming. 'Don't sift. Don't measure. Don't talk. Don't question.'

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I never said don't question. I said don't overthink. Two very different things.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: To me they feel the same. Both mean 'stop being yourself and be more like Mom.'

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I don't want you to be like your mother. I want you to be like YOU. But calmer.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: This IS me calm. You should see me at work. This is me trying very hard to be gentle.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: This is gentle? I'd hate to see angry. The bowl would probably shatter.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: That's not funny. I'm trying here. You're mocking me for trying.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I'm not mocking. I'm... I'm bad at this. Your grandmother handled emotions. I handle wood.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: You handle wood? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I mean I build things. Fix things. I don't talk things through. I'm a hammer, not a hug.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't need a hug. I need you to not turn every question into a personal attack.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: And I need you to not treat my kitchen like a laboratory where I'm the failed experiment.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I don't see you as failed. I see you as... guarded. And I don't know the password.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: There is no password. Just patience. Which we're both running out of.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Then let's just mix the dough. No more questions. No more explanations. Just mix.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Fine. Butter and sugar first. Cream them until fluffy. I'll watch.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Should I use the hand mixer or the wooden spoon?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: There you go again. Question after question. Can you make one decision on your own?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I CAN make decisions. I just want to respect your preference. That's called being polite.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: My preference is that you stop asking my preference and just DO something.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Fine. Hand mixer it is. Loud and fast. Like my mood right now.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Now you're being passive-aggressive. 'Like my mood.' Everything is a statement about me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Not everything is about you. Sometimes it's just about the mixer.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: But you made it about your mood. Which is about our conversation. Which is about me.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Okay. I'm using the mixer because it's efficient. No metaphor. No subtext. Just efficiency.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Efficiency. Good. Finally a reason I understand.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Butter and sugar are creamed. Now what?

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Add the egg. One. Not two. Your mother always tried to add two and it made them cakey.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I wasn't going to add two. I was going to add one. Because that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I said it because I assumed you'd add two. You always do extra. Extra questions, extra effort.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Extra effort is bad now? I thought hard work was a virtue.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: In cookies, extra effort makes them tough. In life, it makes you tired. Both are bad.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: So I should be lazy? Undercook the cookies and underachieve in life? Great advice.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: There's a difference between lazy and relaxed. You've never learned the difference.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Because you never taught it. You taught work ethic. 'Get up early. Stay busy. Don't waste time.'

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I taught that because the world is hard. But in my kitchen, on a Saturday, you can breathe.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'm trying to breathe. But every breath gets analyzed. 'Why are you breathing like that?'

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I never said that. You're putting words in my mouth again.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Not words. Feelings. The feeling that I can't do anything right in this kitchen.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You're doing fine. The butter and sugar look good. See? Progress.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Progress. Like I'm a project. A renovation. 'Granddaughter 2.0: Now With Less Anxiety.'

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You're twisting everything. I said progress because we're making dough. Literal progress.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Maybe. But it's hard to tell when your compliments feel like evaluations.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Evaluations? 'Looks good' is an evaluation now? What would you prefer? A standing ovation?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I'd prefer you say it like you mean it. Not like you're checking a box.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I DO mean it. But you don't believe me. So what's the point of saying anything?

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: The point is connection. But we're not connecting. We're co-existing in the same flour cloud.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: Flour cloud. That's almost poetic. Didn't know you had that in you.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I have a lot in me. You just never ask. You assume you know what's in me.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: What's in you then? Tell me. I'm asking now.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Fear. That I'm losing you. That every visit is a test I fail. That one day you'll stop answering the door.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: I'll always answer the door. But I can't promise I'll be good company. I'm old and cranky.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Cranky I can handle. It's the wall I can't climb. The wall that says 'you don't understand me.'

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You don't understand me either. You think I'm lonely. I'm not. I'm just... used to alone.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: Used to alone is just lonely with better PR.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: PR? Now you're marketing my emotions? I'm not a brand, young lady.

utterances.speaker: granddaughter
utterances.text: I didn't mean it like that. I meant... alone becomes a habit. And habits are hard to break.

utterances.speaker: grandfather
utterances.text: You want to break my habit? My habit is my life. You want to break my life?
